questions.q: According to this lesson, what should happen before writing any KQL for a custom workbook?
options: Write the parameter step before anything else, always
Pick a chart color scheme
State the specific question the workbook needs to answer
Disable every data connector first
questions.explain: A workbook built without a clear question in mind tends to turn into a cluttered dashboard -- one question, one clear chart, one way to narrow it down.

questions.q: In the Sign-in Logs table, what does a ResultType of "0" mean, and why does the lesson's query filter on `ResultType != "0"`?
options: ResultType "0" means the sign-in succeeded, so excluding it leaves only failed sign-ins
ResultType "0" means the log entry is corrupted and should always be discarded
ResultType has no defined meaning and the filter is arbitrary
ResultType "0" means the sign-in came from an unknown location
questions.explain: A ResultType of "0" indicates a successful sign-in, so filtering it out with != "0" isolates failures without having to list every failure code.

questions.q: What does `bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)` do in the failed-login query?
options: Converts TimeGenerated into a text string
Limits the query to exactly one result row
Deletes all rows older than one hour
Groups rows into one-hour time buckets, giving render timechart a time axis to plot
questions.explain: bin() groups timestamps into fixed buckets -- here, one-hour buckets -- which is the time-plus-count shape a timechart needs to draw a trend.

questions.q: What is `{TargetUser}` in the workbook's query step?
options: A comment that KQL ignores when running the query
A hardcoded username that can never be changed
Syntax that substitutes a parameter's current value into the query before it runs
A KQL function that returns the currently logged-in analyst's name
questions.explain: {TargetUser} is how a workbook query step reads a parameter's current value -- whatever the reader selects gets substituted in before the query runs.

questions.q: What does adding a short text step at the top of this workbook accomplish?
options: It is required before any query step can run at all
It explains what the chart shows and how to use the parameter, so a new analyst doesn't have to decode it alone
It automatically fixes any errors in the underlying KQL query
It changes the data connector the workbook is reading from
questions.explain: A one- or two-line text step ties the chart and parameter together, turning the workbook into something a new analyst can use without asking anyone.
